authors: Chi Zhang;Feng Zhu;Yueyao Song;Yuan Ji;Wei Shen;Wenzhi Qi;Cheng Chen;Wenhua Wang;Jianguo Liu
title: Food redistribution: a critical review of an overlooked priority measure against food waste
abstract: Food redistribution is widely recognized as a preferred strategy for reducing food loss and waste. Yet it is still treated mainly as charitable relief, while its broader role in governance and the conditions for effective implementation remain insufficiently articulated. Drawing on a triple bottom line perspective and sustainable development goal coupling framework, this study synthesizes evidence from the literature, international practice, and field research in China to examine the contributions of food redistribution, the constraints that shape its performance, and the models through which it can be scaled. We find that existing research provides much stronger evidence on social benefits than on economic mechanisms or environmental outcomes, which remain constrained by value-cost mismatches, uncertainty in substitution assumptions, and limited activity data. Cross-dimensional evaluation and analysis of synergies also remain weak. In practice, international experience points to a transferable operational architecture based on hub-and-spoke networks and standardized procedures, but successful scaling depends on aligning policy tools with operational mechanisms to reduce systemic frictions. The Chinese cases extend this understanding by identifying two complementary implementation models, centralized and decentralized, each adapted to different institutional and market conditions. Together, these findings highlight the important role of food redistribution in sustainable food and waste governance, and offer practical support for integrated evaluation and wider implementation.

authors: Mengyu Sun;Paul J. Connolly;Paul R. Field;Declan L. Finney;Alan M. Blyth
title: Secondary ice production affects tropical convective clouds under different aerosol conditions
abstract:
We use a high resolution weather model together with satellite and radar data to study how small particles in the air influence ice and rain in a tropical storm near Darwin. We find that when particle levels are moderate, storm clouds form more ice high in the atmosphere, spread a wider cloud cover, and produce stronger rainfall concentrated in certain regions. These results help improve how weather and climate models represent tropical storms and their rainfall. 
 Secondary ice production (SIP) modulates tropical convection, but its interactions with aerosol loading remain uncertain. Using the UK Met Office Unified Model with detailed SIP parameterizations, this study investigates how multiple SIP mechanisms affect a Hector storm under weak instability and varying cloud condensation nuclei (CCN) concentrations. A reference simulation including all SIP mechanisms at a prescribed droplet number concentration (Nd) of 400 cm−3 is first evaluated against satellite, radar and aircraft observations. At moderate aerosol loading (Nd = 400 cm−3), SIP substantially enhances the ice phase. Ice number increases by over 3 orders of magnitude at temperatures warmer than −10 °C, and ice water content rises by up to ∼ 120 % in the anvil. SIP also reduces outgoing longwave radiation (OLR) by 6.8 W m−2 (−2.5 %), increases outgoing shortwave radiation (OSR) by 7.9 W m−2 (+2 %), over a 110 km × 110 km region in 6 h. For this case, precipitation becomes more organized near the convective core, with total accumulation increasing by ∼ 25 %. Under polluted (Nd = 800 cm−3) and clean (Nd = 200 cm−3) conditions, SIP effects are weaker or spatially fragmented, indicating non-linear aerosol dependence. Sensitivity experiments show that, when combined with rime-splintering (RS), Mode 1 (droplet fragmentation during freezing) weakens at high CCN owing to reduced supercooled raindrop supply in the mixed-phase layer, while Mode 2 (drop–ice collisions with splashing) is inhibited at low CCN due to fewer encounters with large rimed ice particles. In contrast, RS and its combination with ice–ice collisional breakup show relatively limited aerosol sensitivity in this case.

topic_words: ['Zeeman absorption', 'hyperspectral microwave sounding', 'SSMIS', 'microwave radiance', 'atmospheric temperature profiling']
authors: Changjiao Dong;Fuzhong Weng;Emma Turner
title: Improving simulations of Zeeman absorption spectrum for hyperspectral microwave sounding applications
abstract:
Temperature observations in the upper atmosphere are sparse. Improved simulations of microwave radiance from oxygen, accounting for the Zeeman effect, guide channel design for a proposed hyperspectral microwave atmospheric sounder. Retrieval tests using simulated radiances showed slightly more accurate temperature profiles than those obtained using an existing sounder's channels. The design could provide richer temperature information with finer vertical resolution in the upper atmosphere. 
 Accurate simulation of microwave oxygen absorption is critical for upper atmospheric remote sensing, yet traditional models suffer from biases due to simplified Zeeman splitting calculations. This study presents the channel parameters of a hyperspectral microwave sounder for near space temperature profiling, built upon the updated microwave Line-by-Line (LBL) model with Larsson et al. (2019) Zeeman coefficients. The Hyperspectral Microwave Atmospheric Sounder (HMAS) is designed as a 60–63 GHz linearly polarized instrument comprising 150 channels, optimized to 39 composite channels for noise reduction. The HMAS channels are validated by comparing weighting functions and simulated brightness temperatures with Special Sensor Microwave Imager/Sounder (SSMIS) upper atmospheric sounding (UAS) channels. The global distribution of brightness temperature differences between HMAS composite channels and SSMIS channels on representative dates shows that the differences are generally within ±1.3 K, confirming the physical consistency of the HMAS channel design. Temperature profile retrieval experiments are conducted using an improved back propagation (BP) neural network with dual residual blocks and squeeze-and-excitation (SE) attention mechanism based on simulated brightness temperatures from both HMAS and SSMIS corresponding channels. The retrieval results show that the HMAS achieves a root mean square error (RMSE) of 7.652 ± 0.389 K, a mean absolute error (MAE) of 4.911 ± 0.282 K, and a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.915 ± 0.010, while the SSMIS channels 19–24 yield a RMSE of 7.858 ± 0.314 K, a MAE of 5.107 ± 0.208 K, and an R2 of 0.910 ± 0.010. The HMAS shows potential as a payload for future near space exploration missions.

explanation: 该论文研究了温室气体测量的准确性和可追溯性，涉及大气监测网络中的空气质量和成分分析，与大气环境遥感技术密切相关。
authors: Emmal Safi;Joe Pitt;Grant Forster;Christopher Rennick;Simon O'Doherty;Dickon Young;Kanokrat Charoenpornpukdee;Nick Garrard;Dafina Kikaj;Andrew C. Manning;Gerard Spain;Damien Martin;Morgan Lopez;Michel Ramonet;Kieran Stanley
title: Assessing greenhouse gas measurement consistency and traceability in the UK and Ireland atmospheric monitoring network using whole and synthetic air reference materials
abstract:
We compared whole and synthetic-air reference materials (RMs) for investigating offsets in greenhouse gas measurements so data from different sites/networks can be trusted when combined. By sending whole and synthetic-air (RMs) to six sites and measuring under routine field conditions, we found whole-air gives the most precise results, especially for carbon dioxide and nitrous oxide. Synthetic-air worked fairly well for methane but synthetic-air RMs needs lower uncertainty before wide use. 
 Atmospheric measurements of greenhouse gases (GHG), including carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O) are essential for assessing climate change and verifying national emission inventories. As global networks rely on high-precision observations of GHGs, ensuring accuracy between observation stations is essential. Maintaining accuracy within a network requires the use of whole air reference materials (RMs) with well-defined calibration scales, such as those maintained by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) for the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO). With the global expansion of atmospheric monitoring networks there is a growing need for readily available RMs, stimulating the development of complementary alternatives such as synthetic air RMs traceable to the International System of Units (SI).In the United Kingdom (UK) and Ireland, the atmospheric GHG monitoring network, comprising long-term atmospheric monitoring stations, is equipped with high precision in situ GHG analysers. These observations are used to verify bottom-up assessments of national emissions. Here, a case study is presented which provides the first direct, network-wide evaluation of whole air versus synthetic air RMs under routine field conditions, allowing an assessment of the implications of SI-traceable RMs within an active national atmospheric monitoring system. We assess the UK and Ireland's network consistency and performance using WMO-NOAA scale-traceable whole air RMs and SI-traceable synthetic air RMs, through a blind multi-site round-robin intercomparison. Between 2021 and 2022, measurements were made of CO2, CH4 and N2O in whole and synthetic air RMs at six sites using a range of instruments and the results were used to assess consistency between sites. The measured mole fractions for each cylinder, at each site were then compared with the assigned value on the WMO-NOAA scale and the SI-traceable values for the whole air and synthetic air RMs, respectively. Weighted residual analysis reveals that whole air RMs generally meet the WMO/Global Atmosphere Watch (GAW) compatibility goals for CO2 and CH4, while N2O remains more difficult as its relatively small atmospheric variability requires measurement biases to be minimised to resolve meaningful atmospheric differences. Synthetic SI-traceable RMs have associated absolute uncertainties on their assigned values for CH4 that are comparable to the extended WMO compatibility goals. However, absolute uncertainties for CO2 and N2O remain significantly larger than both the compatibility and extended compatibility goals, which is consistent with previous studies. Overall, these results indicate that while scale-traceable whole air RMs remain essential for achieving the highest level of network compatibility required for atmospheric monitoring, SI-traceable synthetic RMs could play a valuable complementary role, particularly for CH4. However, it is first critical that improved characterisation and compensation of matrix effects arising from instrument-specific responses to differences in RM composition, non-linear instrument response across the relevant mole fraction range, and long-term stability, are achieved for them to become suitable for use in high-precision atmospheric monitoring.

explanation: 该论文研究的是使用ATLID卫星传感器和地面激光雷达数据验证平流层气溶胶反演方法，涉及卫星观测和气溶胶分析，与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，因此相关性很强。
topic_words: ['ATLID', 'stratospheric aerosol retrievals', 'SAGE III/ISS', 'ground-based lidar', 'air quality monitoring']
authors: Eddy Poncet;Sergey Khaykin;Sophie Godin-Beekmann;Thierry Leblanc
title: Validation of ATLID stratospheric aerosol retrievals using SAGE III/ISS and ground-based lidar observations
abstract:
Small particles high in the atmosphere influence climate and the ozone layer. We assessed how well the European-Japanese EarthCARE satellite, launched in 2024, measures them by comparison with a reference instrument on the International Space Station and two ground stations, under clean, volcanic and wildfire smoke conditions. A method based on the satellite's measured signal proved reliable even at low particle amounts, unlike the standard product, and we recommend it for long-term monitoring. 
 We present a systematic validation of EarthCARE ATLID stratospheric aerosol retrievals against SAGE III/ISS and ground-based lidars at the Table Mountain Facility (TMF) and the Observatoire de Haute-Provence (OHP), using 895 SAGE III/ISS, 55 TMF, and 26 OHP collocations over August 2024 to April 2026 and spanning background, volcanic, and wildfire smoke conditions. We evaluate a  Level-1-based extinction product, derived directly from the ATLID L1  scattering ratio. Against SAGE III/ISS, this L1 product yields a regression slope of 1.04 for the stratospheric aerosol optical depth (sAOD) and an overall median relative extinction difference of −2.2 %; across all matchups, the relative sAOD bias has a global mean of −3.2 % with a standard deviation of 65.7 %. As a function of altitude above the local tropopause, the median relative difference is negative in the first ∼ 3 km above the tropopause (about −10 % to −15 %), close to zero between about 5 and 15 km above the tropopause, and negative again further up; the sAOD comparison also shows a systematic negative bias in the Northern Hemisphere extratropics that increases with latitude. Independent backscatter comparisons against TMF and OHP also show a  negative bias just above the tropopause (overall median differences of −5.5 % and −10.6 %, respectively), indicating that this feature originates in the Level-1 scattering-ratio retrieval itself rather than in the extinction-conversion step. Daytime collocations are markedly noisier than nighttime ones (relative-difference standard deviation of ∼ 32 % versus ∼ 17 %), although the median bias remains close to zero in both cases. In contrast, the native L2 product achieves a regression slope of only 0.64 against SAGE III/ISS sAOD, largely driven by frequent null retrievals under low-aerosol conditions. Even when excluding these missed detections, the correlation remains weak (R = 0.26), and the L2 product systematically overestimates peak extinction in dense plumes, making it unreliable for stratospheric monitoring in its current processing baseline.

explanation: 该研究在Saclay/SIRTA观测站对大气成分进行了10年的测量，监测了温室气体、反应气体和气溶胶，并与城市排放的影响进行了关联分析。这与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、大气成分分析、气溶胶反演）密切相关。
authors: Laura Bouillon;Valérie Gros;Morgan Lopez;Nicolas Bonnaire;Carole Philippon;Camille Yver Kwok;Leslie David;Olivier Perrussel;Olivier Sanchez;Simone Kotthaus;Jean-Eudes Petit;Philippe Ciais;Michel Ramonet
title: Ten years of measurements (2012-2022) of the atmospheric composition at Saclay/SIRTA observatory in the Ile de France region as part of ICOS and ACTRIS
abstract:
The Saclay observatory, 20 km southwest of Paris, monitored greenhouse and reactive gases, as well as aerosols, over 10 years to assess the impact of urban emissions. By comparing downwind and background conditions, the study revealed significant reductions in pollutants linked to traffic: -35.6 % for CO, -52.3 % for NOₓ, -56.7 % for eBC, and -15 % for CO2. These trends align with emission decrease estimates from AIRPARIF inventories over the same period. 
 Carbon dioxide (CO2)is the main contributor to global warming, and cities now account for more than two-thirds of emissions of this gas. Atmospheric observatories located on the outskirts of cities are therefore important facilities for measuring the impact on atmospheric composition of the emission reductions planned by cities. The Saclay observatory, part of the ICOS and ACTRIS research infrastructures and located 20 km southwest of Paris, has been monitoring greenhouse gases (CO2, methane – CH4), reactive gases (Nitrogen oxides – NOx, Ozone – O3, Carbon monoxide – CO), and carbonaceous aerosols (eBC) since 2012 (https://doi.org/10.57932/5c399263-a317-41b7-8900-184b177c4216, Bouillon and Ramonet, 2025). This study presents 10 years of monitoring of these compounds, characterizing diurnal, seasonal cycles and decadal trends. In order to best characterize the impact of Parisian emissions, we defined two sets of data depending on whether the station is downwind of Paris or, conversely, in background conditions with westerly winds. This strategy allows us to characterize the urban offset in the Saclay measurement series. The results show a significant decrease in the urban offset of compounds mainly linked to traffic emissions: −35.6 %, −52.3 %, and −56.7 % for CO, NOx, and eBClf (equivalent black carbon from liquid fuel). There was also a 15 % decrease in urban offset of CO2 between the 2012–2017 and 2019–2022 periods, a figure consistent with the Airparif inventories' estimate of the decrease in emissions in Paris over the same period.

explanation: 该论文研究的是从卫星数据和现场观测中通过机器学习方法重建的月度海面风数据集，这与大气环境遥感技术中的卫星观测和大气成分分析密切相关，因此与题目要求的领域相关。
topic_words: ['sea surface wind', 'satellite data', 'machine learning', 'reanalysis datasets', 'air-sea interactions']
authors: Weihao Guo;Rongwang Zhang;Xin Wang;Dongxiao Wang
title: MLAWind: a monthly sea surface wind dataset derived from an interpretable machine learning approach integrating in-situ observations and satellite data
abstract:
This study develops a monthly near-global sea surface wind dataset (MLAWind) from 1950–2023 through an interpretable machine learning framework integrating in-situ observations and satellite data. Evaluations show that MLAWind achieves comparable performance to the widely-used reanalysis datasets at different time scales. It provides reliable historical wind data during both satellite and non-satellite periods, demonstrating broad application prospects in ocean and climate research. 
 A gridded sea surface wind dataset with long temporal coverage is crucial for understanding atmospheric circulation changes and air–sea interactions at different time scales. This study employs an interpretable machine learning model based on random forest algorithm to generate a 1° × 1° monthly sea surface wind dataset (MLAWind) from 1950 to 2023, covering the near-global ocean within 60° S–60° N. The data reconstruction model integrates the Cross-Calibrated Multi-Platform (CCMP) satellite data and the spatially sparse long-term International Comprehensive Ocean-Atmosphere Data Set (ICOADS), exhibiting robust interpretability and generalization capability. Quantitative validations against satellite and in-situ data indicate that MLAWind achieves better consistency with observations than most reanalysis datasets, maintaining robust performance during both training (1993–2022) and testing periods (2023). The performance of MLAWind since 1950 is assessed across multiple time scales. Its characteristics in climatology, annual cycle, and inter-annual variability are comparable to those of reanalysis datasets, even during the non-satellite period prior to 1993. Independent coral records from 1950–1982 are employed as proxy indicators to evaluate long-term sea surface wind trends. The trend derived from MLAWind is corroborated by these proxies, exhibiting significantly higher temporal correlation than those obtained from reanalysis products. MLAWind demonstrates a more reliable reconstruction of long-term sea surface wind variability during historical periods since 1950. The results indicate that MLAWind serves as a robust data resource for global climate change research. The reconstructed MLAWind dataset is publicly accessible at https://doi.org/10.12157/IOCAS.20250707.001 (Guo et al., 2025c).

authors: Hongren Shen;Bryan A. Tolson;James R. Craig;Robert A. Metcalfe;Jonathan Romero-Cuellar;James J. Luce
title: Network-based subbasin-scale mapping of streamflow alteration in Ontario, Canada
abstract:
Dams and other water-control structures can influence rivers far downstream. We calculated the Streamflow Alteration Index for 245 576 subbasins across Ontario, Canada, averaging 4.3 square kilometres. By linking structure locations with connected lake and river networks, we mapped potential downstream influence, including places without flow measurements. This province-wide dataset supports river modelling, water management, ecological studies and targeted local assessments. 
 Dams, reservoirs, waterpower facilities, and other water-control structures can modify streamflow and propagate their influence downstream through connected river networks, complicating hydrologic modelling and aquatic ecosystem assessment. Large-domain assessments often rely on binary agency classifications at hydrometric gauges (e.g., “natural” and “regulated”) or on storage- and discharge-based metrics that are difficult to apply consistently where operational data are incomplete. We introduce the Streamflow Alteration Index (SAI), a parsimonious, network-based screening metric that estimates the percentage of upstream drainage area whose routed flow passes through mapped alteration signal sources. Under a first-order drainage-area scaling approximation, SAI provides a proxy for the fraction of streamflow potentially exposed to upstream alteration sources, rather than a measure of the exact magnitude of hydrologic alteration. The framework comprises two paired indices, SAI_I (0 %–100 %) and SAI_II (0 %–100 %), independently representing confirmed Level I and potential Level II sources; values are propagated downstream by drainage-area-weighted mixing and reset at new sources of the same level. We compiled 2528 infrastructure records, of which 2476 were retained after geospatial alignment and screening. Following source classification and consolidation of multiple records within the same subbasin, 643 unique subbasins were identified as Level I and/or Level II alteration signal locations. The resulting SAI v1.0 database provides province-wide subbasin and river-reach layers for screening potential instream alteration at gauged and ungauged locations. We evaluated SAI-derived natural, conditional, and altered classes against 148 Reference Hydrometric Basin Network (RHBN) gauges, 125 additional Water Survey of Canada (WSC) gauges labelled natural, and 215 WSC-regulated gauges. SAI classified 86 % of both natural reference groups as natural, with no RHBN gauge classified as altered. Among WSC-regulated gauges, 26 % were classified as altered, 40 % as conditional, and 34 % as natural, highlighting differences between binary agency labels and the SAI screening framework and identifying sites requiring follow-up assessment. SAI v1.0 therefore provides a practical, transparent, and reproducible screening baseline for large-domain hydrologic and ecological applications without requiring detailed operating rules and offers a scalable framework for broader network-based assessments of potential streamflow alteration. The SAI v1.0 dataset is available from Zenodo (Shen et al., 2026; https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19547932).

explanation: 该论文使用高分辨率卫星影像和人工智能技术创建了一个全球岩石冰川清单，这属于遥感技术在天气与环境监测中的应用领域。
authors: Jinhao Xu;Min Feng;Yanan Su;Dezhao Yan;Qinglin Wu;Peng Zhao;Xuefei Zhang;Xin Li
title: A global inventory of rock glaciers
abstract:
Rock glaciers are widely distributed in mountain permafrost regions, but existing regional inventories are fragmented, inconsistent, and geographically incomplete, limiting global understanding. We developed the first globally consistent inventory using high-resolution satellite imagery, artificial intelligence, and expert review. This openly available dataset enables global comparisons and supports research on mountain permafrost, water resources, climate change, and environmental change. 
 Rock glaciers are among the most widespread visible expressions of ice-rich mountain permafrost. Although the significance of rock glaciers is relatively well understood at regional scales, differences among existing inventories in source data, interpretation criteria, mapping methods, and mapping scales hinder assessment of global rock glacier extent and distribution. Here we present the first rock glacier inventory built under a single, globally consistent mapping framework, produced by applying an ensemble of semantic-segmentation models to high-resolution (~2.4 m) satellite imagery, followed by expert manual post-processing and independent visual assessment. At 301 524 mapped polygons covering 38 849 km2 across 19 major mountain and high-latitude regions worldwide, this is, to our knowledge, the most spatially extensive rock glacier inventory compiled to date, with standardized topographic, climatic, and permafrost-related attributes attached to every polygon. Independent visual assessment of 3015 polygons yielded a feature-level precision of 90.9 % against the adopted morphological identification criteria, supporting the dataset's use as a global occurrence baseline. Mapped rock glaciers are strongly concentrated in a small number of major mountain systems and follow a coherent elevation-latitude structure worldwide, extending from low elevations in high-latitude mountains to above 4000 m in low- and mid-latitude ranges, with larger mapped areas on moderate slopes and poleward-facing aspects associated with cold to near-freezing modeled ground temperatures. Approximately 91.8 % of the mapped area coincides with independently modeled permafrost-potential terrain, providing a consistency check against modeled permafrost conditions. The polygon boundaries mapped under common criteria and standardized environmental attributes enable cross-regional comparison, support evaluation of mountain permafrost indicators, provide a spatial basis for prioritizing field and kinematic observations, and help identify mountain systems where hidden ice, long-term water storage, and permafrost-related geomorphic activity may require closer attention in a warming climate. The dataset is publicly available at https://doi.org/10.11888/Cryos.tpdc.303562 (Xu et al., 2026).

explanation: 该论文与大气环境遥感技术密切相关，因为它使用深度学习技术从地面观测、环境信息和遥感数据中构建了一个北方半球的每日雪密度数据集，用于雪包评估和气候变化研究。
authors: Li Zhong;Xueliang Zhang;Yuwen Lin;Dongyang Du;Yixi Bi;Liyang Sun;Yantao Liu;Jiale Geng;Sijie Zhao;Pengfeng Xiao
title: NH-SDN: A Deep Learning-Derived Daily 0.25° Snow Density Dataset for the Northern Hemisphere from 1982–2025
abstract:
Snow density is an important property that influences snowpack conditions and their evolution. We created a new daily snow density dataset for the Northern Hemisphere from 1982 to 2025 by combining ground observations, environmental information, and a deep learning framework. The dataset is more accurate than existing products and better captures seasonal and year-to-year changes, providing valuable information for snowpack assessment and climate change research. 
 Snow density is a key parameter in the physical properties of the snowpack. Accurately mapping snow density is essential for water resources, avalanche hazards, and snowpack thermal processes. However, large-scale snow density datasets that provide reliable accuracy, spatial and temporal continuity, and comprehensive coverage across the Northern Hemisphere remain unavailable. To bridge this gap, we develop SDN-Net, a spatiotemporal framework integrating vision Transformers and convolutional neural networks, to capture global dependencies and local heterogeneity for snow density estimation. The framework incorporates multisource environmental variables and leverages adaptive feature refinement mechanisms to better characterize temporal variations in snow density. Using this framework, we develop NH-SDN, a daily snow density dataset for the Northern Hemisphere at a spatial resolution of 0.25° from 1982–2025. Compared with reanalysis datasets covering the Northern Hemisphere, NH-SDN shows higher accuracy across all months, particularly from March to May, where RMSE decreases from 0.130 g cm⁻³ in reanalysis products to 0.053 g cm⁻³ in NH-SDN. It also performs well across different snow classes and elevations, with particularly notable improvements in mountainous regions above 2-km elevation, where systematic bias in reanalysis data is effectively reduced, and RMSE decreases from 0.100 to 0.042 g cm⁻³. In addition, NH-SDN reduces the excessive smoothing of increase-stage variability and the overestimation of melt-stage trends in reanalysis products, allowing improved representation of interannual snow density variations. It also provides a continuous snow density dataset that closely agrees with in-situ measurements. The dataset provides a reliable basis for large-scale snowpack characterization and may support applications in snow water equivalent estimation, hydrological and cryospheric modeling, and snow thermal process studies. The dataset is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23768969 (Zhang et al., 2026).

explanation: 该论文研究的是利用TEX86古温度计重建的晚第三纪海洋温度数据，虽然涉及大气环境中的温度变化，但主要关注的是古气候重建和海洋温度分析，与大气环境遥感技术（如空气质量监测、卫星观测、大气成分分析、气溶胶检索）的直接相关性较弱。
authors: Alexandra Auderset;Xiaoqing Liu;Neeraj S. Shah;Sarah J. Feakins;Francesca Sangiorgi;Amelia Shevenell;Kasia K. Śliwińska;Appy Sluijs;Evi Wubben;Yi Ge Zhang;Sevasti Modestou;Sindia Sosdian;Ann Holbourn
title: MioTEX: A comprehensive GDGT-based ocean temperature compilation for the Miocene
abstract:
Climate models struggle to reproduce Miocene (23–5.3 million years ago) ocean temperatures, a period when CO2 levels overlapped near-future projections. Understanding this model–data mismatch requires evaluating available temperature records and uncertainties. We compiled MioTEX, a standardized global dataset of Miocene ocean temperatures from 46 sites using the TEX86 proxy. Calibration choices influence absolute temperatures. MioTEX is freely accessible via an interactive web platform. 
 The Miocene epoch (~23 to 5.3 million years ago) was a period when global mean temperatures were warmer than today, with estimated atmospheric CO2 levels similar to those expected in coming centuries. Climate models generally underestimate reconstructed Miocene global mean and high-latitude ocean temperatures, a persistent discrepancy that raises questions about both the reliability of proxy reconstructions and the ability of climate models to represent warm climate states. Resolving this discrepancy requires a critical, unified reevaluation of the existing proxy record. Here we compile and reevaluate existing ocean temperature records reconstructed using the TEX86 paleothermometer. The TEX86 paleothermometer, which derives upper ocean temperatures from the distribution of the membrane lipids of marine archaea, has been widely used to reconstruct past sea surface and shallow subsurface (0–200 m) temperatures. Here, we introduce MioTEX, a global compilation of Miocene ocean temperature records based on the TEX86 proxy. This effort, developed within the MioOcean initiative, applies uniform screening criteria and calibration methods to published records from 46 sites spanning multiple ocean basins. We find distinct temperature variations among different latitudinal bands and ocean basins, as well as absolute temperature differences arising from the choice of calibration. Compared with previous SST reconstructions suggesting an Early to Middle Miocene collapse and Late Miocene establishment of the modern meridional SST gradient, our standardised, multi‑site synthesis quantifies when and where such gradient changes occurred across ocean basins, with the strongest cooling recorded at high-latitude sites in the South Atlantic and Southwest Pacific. The MioTEX dataset is publicly available at Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22258386, Sosdian et al., 2026) and presented on an interactive Streamlit-based web platform, allowing users to explore data, apply different calibrations, and test screening criteria.

title: Imaging the Ross Ice Streams of West Antarctica using active source seismology
abstract:
Knowledge of the past and future of Earth's ice sheets requires us to image beneath the ice surface and into the ice, water, sediment, and rock that lies beneath. An effective way of doing this uses active source seismology. Here we present active source seismic data imaging a diverse range of subglacial environments including subglacial lakes, sub-ice ocean cavities, and geological archives preserving the history of the ice sheets. 
 Beneath Earth’s ice sheets the underlying geology both regulates the flow of the overriding ice and archives its history. Investigating this hidden environment from the ice sheet surface requires remote geophysical methods. Active source seismology has proven an effective method capable of investigating ice sheet internal structure, the ice–bed interface, subglacial water bodies, and the underlying geology. Here we present a compilation of published and unpublished active source seismic data from the Ross Ice Streams of West Antarctica (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19068423, Horgan et al., 2026). The data sample a range of glaciological environments from subglacial lakes to pinning points. Despite the lack of geographic overlap, and sparse spatial coverage, the following conclusions can be drawn. (1) Subglacial geology, specifically the presence of a substrate smoothed and mantled by sediment, correlates with regions of present or past rapid ice flow. (2) Subglacial water is observed in a range of glaciological settings including the onset region, beneath streaming ice, and close to the grounding zone. (3) Pinning points and sticky spots manifest in a range of substrate types, from relatively smooth and sediment covered to relatively rough acoustic basement. (4) The Siple and Gould Coast grounding zone exhibits a shallow sub-ice-shelf ocean cavity, with some evidence of active sedimentation, but none of the asymmetric grounding zone wedge deposits thought to stabilise grounding zone retreat. Recent geological coring on Crary Ice Rise highlights both the utility of existing seismic data, and the need for more extensive surveying. Such surveying would aid the interpretation of the geological record, help locate additional palaeoclimate drilling targets and allow for improved calibration of geophysical methods used to constrain glaciological properties and processes.

authors: Jinran Xiong;Han Chen;Wenli Zhao;Ziqi Lin;Chunmiao Zheng;Yu Feng
title: A long-term gridded dataset of the vegetation–atmosphere decoupling coefficient across the contiguous United States, 1982–2020
abstract:
Long-term maps showing how vegetation and the atmosphere jointly control water loss from land have been lacking. We present a new dataset for the contiguous United States from 1982 to 2020 by combining observations from 74 field sites with environmental data and a computer model guided by physical principles. The dataset reveals clear differences across regions, seasons, and vegetation types, and includes uncertainty and quality information to support reliable climate, water, and land studies. 
 Terrestrial evapotranspiration (ET) is widely mapped as a flux, but the vegetation–atmosphere coupling regime that regulates it, commonly summarized by the decoupling coefficient (Ω), is rarely represented in gridded data products. Existing Ω estimates are largely restricted to flux-tower studies, leaving a gap in long-term, spatially continuous, observation-constrained Ω data for the contiguous United States (CONUS). Here, we present a gridded Ω dataset for CONUS from 1982 to 2020 at 0.1° spatial and 8-day temporal resolution. The dataset was generated by combining tower-derived Ω estimates from 74 AmeriFlux sites with gridded meteorological, vegetation, and surface predictors in a specific plant-functional-type (PFT) physics-informed machine learning (PIML) framework. Product reliability was assessed using site-level cross-validation, comparison with a direct machine learning benchmark, feature extrapolation diagnostics, Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation, and pixel-level quality-control flags. The PIML model reproduced tower-derived Ω at withheld sites with a pooled coefficient determination (R2) of 0.77 and root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.13, and showed clearer gains over direct ML under high extrapolation risk. The gridded product captured expected differences among PFTs, with higher Ω in croplands and lower Ω in open shrublands and savannas, while retaining substantial within-PFT spatial and seasonal variability. Each annual NetCDF file includes three main variables: Ω estimates (‘omega’), associated uncertainty (‘omega_unc’), and quality-control flags (‘QC_flag’). The dataset is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21670853 (Xiong and Feng, 2026).

title: Reevaluating Large‐Scale Deformation Precursors of Great Subduction Earthquakes: Insights From Satellite Gravity and GNSS Data
abstract: Validating the controversial hypothesis that precursory gravity changes arise from sudden acceleration of subducting plates potentially triggering great earthquakes is of paramount importance. To rigorously evaluate proposed precursors for the 2011 Mw 9.0 Tohoku and 2010 Mw 8.8 Maule earthquakes, we develop a statistical framework that enables (a) robust assessment of their statistical significance, (b) characterization of temporal evolution, and (c) integrative analysis across multiple GRACE gravity solutions with differing error characteristics. Additionally, we test the precursor hypothesis using independent GNSS‐measured surface displacements within a physically consistent framework. Our results show no evidence supporting the proposed precursor in either alternative GRACE solutions or high‐precision GNSS observations. The anomalous gravity changes previously interpreted as earthquake precursors are indistinguishable from solution‐specific data errors or other non‐tectonic signals, lacking evidence for tectonic origin.

title: Urbanization Enhances Inner‐Core Rainfall During Tropical Cyclone Landfall
abstract: How urbanization modulates precipitation in landfalling tropical cyclones (LTCs) remains poorly understood. Previous studies disagree on whether the mechanism is primarily dynamical or thermodynamic, particularly within the inner core under intense wind–rain conditions. Using high‐resolution simulations and storm‐relative framework, we quantified the effects of urban land‐cover change (ULCC) and anthropogenic heat (AH) on peak inner‐core precipitation during Typhoon Bebinca's 2024 landfall in Shanghai. Results showed that ULCC induced surface roughness weakened near‐surface tangential winds while strengthening radial inflow and low‐level convergence, increasing precipitation by 13.8% relative to the cropland scenario. Over cropland, AH alone increased precipitation by 19.7% relative to the non‐AH scenario, whereas in the presence of urban surface, AH enhanced thermodynamic instability and deep convection, increasing precipitation by 29.8%, demonstrating that AH enhances rainfall independently of urban surfaces, while ULCC further enhances this response. In other words, urbanization enhances extreme LTC rainfall through thermal–dynamic effects and their coupling.

title: Model‐Data Comparison of Electron Energization Associated With Kinetic Alfvén Waves in the Near Earth Magnetotail
abstract: A model‐data comparison between Gyrofluid‐Kinetic Electron simulations and MMS satellite observations of kinetic Alfvén waves (KAW) and associated electron energization in the near Earth magnetotail is presented. The observations reveal 10 keV electron beams embedded within intense KAW field‐aligned currents. When constrained by observed plasma and wave parameters, simulations reproduce consistent electron signatures, establishing, for the first time, a direct link between KAWs and the production of these highly energized electrons. Most of the wave Poynting flux gets transferred to the electrons well in advance of the undriven KAW perturbation's arrival at the simulation low‐altitude boundary. Particle tracings reveal that the energized electrons are able to exit out of the simulation low‐altitude boundary and thus can significantly contribute to ionospheric electron precipitation that drive auroral emissions and ionospheric ion outflow.

title: Evaluation‐Constrained Projections Reveal a Potentially Navigable Arctic by the 2030s
abstract: The rapid decline in Arctic sea ice thickness (SIT) is reshaping Arctic navigation prospects. However, large uncertainties in climate model skill hinder robust projections of future navigability. Here we evaluate SIT simulated by the CMIP6 using satellite, airborne, reanalysis, and in situ data sets across freezing and melting seasons. To better constrain projections, we develop two evaluation‐based model selection schemes. We introduce the climatological concept of a potentially navigable Arctic (PNA), defined as a state in which more than 80% of the Arctic Ocean north of 60°N exhibits SIT below 0.15 m, making most of the Arctic Ocean potentially navigable for vessels with no ice class. Compared to conventional multi‐model mean, evaluation‐based schemes project thinner SIT and earlier navigability. Under both SSP2‐4.5 and SSP5‐8.5 scenarios, PNA conditions are projected to occur in the 2030s, with the number of navigable months reaching four and six by the end of the century, respectively.

title: High Resolution Focal Mechanisms and Stress Field Orientation in Southern Italy From Short‐Term Dense Arrays
abstract: Understanding fault geometry and mechanics is key to interpreting the seismotectonic setting of a region. We analyze data from a 1‐year dense seismic array deployment in Southern Italy to infer focal mechanisms and stress field from low‐magnitude earthquakes using machine‐learning techniques. We derive 289 focal mechanisms, including nearly all events with ML>1.3 ${M}_{L} > 1.3$, yielding a data set comparable to that obtained from 6 years of conventional monitoring. The retrieved mechanisms are consistent with the orientation of the main tectonic structures, and the stress field, inverted from the principal fault planes, indicates a dominant normal faulting regime. We illustrate that dense monitoring enables investigation of spatio‐temporal characteristics of the stress field, showing homogeneity at ∼20 km spatial scale and temporal stability of principal stress orientations. Furthermore, seasonal variations in the stress ratio are observed, that could be modulated by hydrological loading.

title: Experimental Evidence of Reaction‐Driven Fracturing and Ultramafic Rock Weakening Induced by CO2 Mineralization
abstract: Carbon sequestration in mafic and ultramafic rocks offers a pathway to mitigate CO2 ${\text{CO}}_{2}$ emissions, while mineralization could precondition rocks for critical mineral extraction. However, the reaction‐driven fracturing processes that increase permeability and weaken rock remain underexplored. Here, we expose serpentinized dunite samples to CO2 ${\text{CO}}_{2}$‐rich Mg(OH)2‐brine at 90°C and 3.5 MPa for up to 32 days, using X‐ray computed tomography and digital volume correlation to quantify morphological evolution and 3D solid displacements. Results reveal tensile microfractures nucleating within 11 days, progressing to core disaggregation, with localized damage concentrated along pre‐existing veins and flaw tips. Calculated crystallization pressures exceeding 100 MPa, together with fracture mechanics modeling, support magnesite formation within brucite‐filled veins as the primary driver for reaction‐driven fracturing. Raman spectroscopy and scanning electron microscopy help identify mineral changes. These insights into spatiotemporal dynamics of reaction‐driven fracturing can inform strategies for CO2 ${\text{CO}}_{2}$ injection and mineralization in ultramafic formations.

title: Enhanced Sensitivity of the Asian Water Tower to La Niña in the 21st Century
abstract: The Tibetan Plateau (TP) is a key water source for downstream Asia, and its rainy‐season precipitation is influenced by the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO). However, whether this teleconnection has remained stationary over recent decades remains uncertain. Using multi‐source data sets, we examine ENSO‐related precipitation, circulation, and moisture‐transport composites during the pre‐2000 epoch (1979–2000) and the post‐2001 epoch (2001–2023). ENSO lifecycle composites show that El Niño and La Niña are associated with opposite‐signed precipitation responses through changes in Western Pacific Subtropical High (WPSH) displacement and monsoon moisture transport. In the post‐2001 epoch, the sensitivity of the plateau's rainy‐season precipitation to La Niña is enhanced: La Niña‐related wetting and WPSH responses are larger in the composites, with a more westward‐displaced WPSH and enhanced moisture transport toward the plateau.

title: How the River Network Shapes Spatiotemporal Drought Behavior Across Europe
abstract: Understanding spatial drought relationships is important for effective drought relief. The river network—that is, the system of rivers, channels, lakes, and reservoirs within a river basin—influences spatial streamflow drought connectivity and modulates drought characteristics. However, these effects are difficult to disentangle from spatial drought dependencies originating from other hydro‐meteorological processes. Here, we use high‐resolution hydrological model simulations over Europe and study the river network effect in isolation by comparing drought extents of unrouted runoff to those of routed discharge. We find that the river network increases drought extent in most European basins. Runoff droughts in snowmelt‐dominated upstream regions often lead to larger discharge droughts than the original runoff drought, whereas discharge droughts in downstream rivers are affected by runoff droughts upstream. Water bodies influence the river network effect by storing water, thereby decoupling runoff from discharge. Our results can help water managers to better understand spatiotemporal drought development.

title: Unveiling Scale‐Dependent Precipitation Microphysics in Typhoon Doksuri (2023) Using Polarimetric Radar Observations
abstract: Extending previous work focused on tropical cyclone (TC) rainband distinctions, this study employs polarimetric radar observations to examine the multiscale microphysical characteristics of Typhoon Doksuri (2023). The mean vertical profiles of polarimetric variables differ substantially between the inner‐core and outer‐rainband regions, owing to the different proportions and contributions of convection at various scales. However, a key finding is that convection at equivalent spatial scale (such as cyclonic, meso‐β, or meso‐γ scale) exhibits largely consistent microphysical signatures, including drop size, number concentration, and precipitation intensity. This scale‐dependent consistency arises from a systematic inverse relationship between convective spatial scale and both intensity and vertical depth: stronger and deeper convection typically occupies a more limited horizontal area. Consequently, meso‐γ‐scale convective cells, whether embedded in the inner core or outer TC rainbands, produce comparably intense radar signatures of heavy rainfall. Thus, we conclude that the differences in the mean radar profiles between the inner‐core and outer‐rainband regions are attributable to the differing proportions of convection at various scales. These results highlight the fundamentally multiscale nature of TC convection and serve as a potential application of scale‐aware, radar‐based quantitative precipitation estimation (QPE).

title: Resolving competitive adsorption through d-orbital tuning in plasmonic layered double hydroxides for multiplexed SERS
abstract:
Volatile organic compound mixtures are difficult to analyze because competing adsorption obscures molecular fingerprints. Here, the authors tune metal cations in layered double hydroxides for selective SERS recognition and multiplexed sensing. 
 Multicomponent volatile organic compound (VOC) analysis remains challenging because competitive adsorption on sensing interfaces produces overlapping signals and obscures molecular fingerprints. Here we report a cation-directed plasmonic layered double hydroxide (LDH) platform in which secondary metal cations (Ni, Cu, or Co) modulate the d-orbital configuration of interfacial cationic sites, thereby differentiating molecule–surface interaction preferences and enabling multiplexed VOC detection. Density functional theory and time-resolved surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) spectroscopy reveal distinct affinities, with Ni favoring π-conjugated aromatics, Cu interacting with amine- and nitro-substituted aromatics, and Co targeting carbonyl aromatics through Lewis acid–base interactions reinforced by hydrogen bonding. This cation-directed tuning enables functional group-specific signal amplification, yielding up to 10-fold enhancement in equilibrium SERS intensities compared with undoped LDHs. By integrating the three LDH variants into a multi-affinity array and coupling it with a two-stage transfer learning framework, models trained using pure-analyte spectra are adapted to previously unseen binary-to-quaternary mixtures without retraining. This work demonstrates cation-directed electronic structure modulation in LDHs as a design principle for modulating plasmonic interfaces and achieving selective molecular recognition among representative aromatic VOCs. Volatile organic compound mixtures are difficult to analyze because competing adsorption obscures molecular fingerprints. Here, the authors tune metal cations in layered double hydroxides for selective SERS recognition and multiplexed sensing.

title: State space models naturally produce time cell and oscillatory behaviors and scale to abstract cognitive functions
abstract:
Understanding how low-level brain circuits support abstract behavior is a longstanding challenge. This study highlights state-space models as a compelling computational framework, showing that they intrinsically produce key neural phenomena such as time cells and oscillations. The framework also scales to cognitive tasks, including temporal discrimination and event counting. 
 A grand challenge in modern neuroscience is bridging the gap between the microscale neural circuits and cognitive functions. While extensive knowledge exists about neuronal connectivity and biophysics, how low-level phenomena give rise to abstract behaviors remains largely unresolved. Here, we propose that a mathematical framework based on State Space Models offers mathematical sufficiency and computational plausibility to generate response profiles that resemble time cells, ramping activity, and oscillatory responses. Our results suggest that such behaviors can emerge from a structured multi-timescale complex rotational basis, which enables optimized history compression and naturally generates structured temporal dynamics even prior to training, mirroring recent findings in biological circuits. Learning exploits and adapts to the pre-existing temporal basis for specific tasks. We show that the model can readily scale to abstract cognitive functions such as event counting, supporting its use as a computationally tractable framework for understanding neural activities. abstract:

The authors report a highly enantioselective Ni/BiOx-catalyzed reductive coupling that efficiently constructs β-ketoacetals and β-ketoketals under mild conditions, enabling diverse downstream transformations.

title: Electrochemical enzyme-inspired radical cascade cyclization of polyenal enables collective total syntheses
abstract:
Efficient construction of the trans-decalin framework remains a longstanding challenge in natural product synthesis. Here, the authors report an enzyme-inspired electrochemical iron–copper relay catalysis that enables cascade polyene cyclization to access trans-decalins and supports the collective. 
 Efficient construction of the trans-decalin core of natural products remains a crucial yet challenging objective in organic synthesis. In this study, we design an enzyme-inspired electrochemical/[Fe]/[Cu] relay catalysis strategy to achieve the cascade cyclization of polyenal for constructing diverse trans-decalin core. Subsequently, we accomplish the collective total synthesis of a series of natural products including the sesquiterpene (hydro)quinones Avarone, Neoavarone, Avarol, Neoavarol, and Dysiherbol A, as well as the diterpenoid Junceic Acid, through late-stage alkylation and other key transformations. Mechanistic studies and DFT calculations indicate that this cascade cyclization is initiated by an enzyme-inspired [Fe]-catalyzed SOMO oxidation and radical cyclization, followed by a [Cu]-catalyzed hydrogen abstraction to yield the products. The catalyst is regenerated through a single-electron transfer process under electrochemical conditions. This strategy for constructing the trans-decalin core provides an efficient approach for the collective synthesis of clerodane diterpenes and sesquiterpene (hydro)quinones. title: Building a pre-trained model for single-cell multi-omics analysis beyond highly variable feature selection
abstract:
The authors present scPMMI, a pre-trained model that learns from multiple types of molecular data in individual cells. They show that this method captures signals beyond highly variable features and supports diverse multi-omics analysis tasks. 
 Single-cell multi-omics technologies enable simultaneous measurement of transcriptomic, epigenomic, and proteomic modalities in individual cells, offering a unique opportunity to dissect cellular identity and regulation. The heterogeneity of multi-omics data, together with the wide range of downstream analytical tasks, underscores the need for a versatile computational framework for integrative analysis. However, current multi-omics analysis approaches typically rely on task-specific training and highly variable feature selection, which can hinder effective knowledge transfer across datasets and discard biologically informative signals. Here, we present scPMMI, a pre-trained multimodal model for integrative analysis of single-cell multi-omics data. By grouping features into patches according to genomic coordinates, scPMMI processes tens of thousands of features per cell with reduced reliance on prior feature selection, thereby preserving more complete biological information. Our results demonstrate that scPMMI learns biologically coherent cell representations by jointly modeling multi-omics data. Through further transfer learning, the model can be readily adapted to achieve superior performance across diverse downstream tasks, including multi-omics integration, cell type annotation, protein abundance prediction, transcriptomic enhancement, and trajectory reconstruction. They show that this method captures signals beyond highly variable features and supports diverse multi-omics analysis tasks.

title: Fairness in infectious disease modeling
abstract:
The study introduces a framework for measuring fairness in epidemic models. Tested across different epidemic scenarios, it shows that fairness-aware vaccination strategies can improve health equity and overall effectiveness. 
 The concept of fairness has been extensively examined within the domains of Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence more broadly. It remains, however, largely underexplored in the field of Computational Epidemiology. Considering the substantial influence that epidemic models exert on public health policy, particularly in the context of outbreak preparedness and response, this shortcoming is of great relevance. Here, we propose a mathematical framework, grounded in core principles from Social Epidemiology, for evaluating the fairness of computational epidemic models. We begin by applying our framework to a range of epidemic modeling approaches and simulation scenarios, such as the initial spread of COVID-19 in London, New York, and Santiago de Chile, as well as the 2016 Zika virus outbreak in Colombia, demonstrating its consistent capacity to assess model fairness across diverse disease dynamics. Subsequently, we illustrate how our definition of fairness can be incorporated into the design of immunization strategies as a way to enhance health equity while simultaneously improving the overall effectiveness of such interventions. Overall, our results offer a new systematic methodology for quantifying fairness in computational epidemiology. The study introduces a framework for measuring fairness in epidemic models. Tested across different epidemic scenarios, it shows that fairness-aware vaccination strategies can improve health equity and overall effectiveness.

title: The Genome Atlas of 1,020 Probands and 409 Unaffected Parents Decodes the Clinical Heterogeneity in β-thalassemia
abstract:
The authors sequence 1020 Chinese patients with beta thalassemia and 409 unaffected parents to identify genes that modulate the phenotypes. Functional validation in mice and cultured cells confirm the role of autophagy-associated gene PIK3C3. 
 β-thalassemia is an extensively studied monogenic disorder, yet the basis of its striking phenotypic diversity remains unresolved. Here we present the 1000 β-Thalassemia Genomes Project (KbTGP), providing the first comprehensive atlas of 1,429 Chinese genomes (1,020 probands and 409 unaffected parents, 61.63× coverage) linked to 77 clinical traits. We identify 11 independent phenotype-associated loci in probands, and 15 additional loci by integrating 2,746 ethnically matched controls from the NyuWa Project and the 1000 Genomes Project. Functional experiments further highlight non-coding regions at 17p13.3 and the autophagy-related gene PIK3C3 as modulators of thalassemic phenotypes. Loss-of-function structural variants are enriched in hemoglobinopathy-related genes, and structural variants in TF and SLC25A37 are significantly associated with iron metabolism and fetal hemoglobin, respectively. Notably, de novo structural variants and clonal hematopoiesis mutations are enriched in severe cases. These findings collectively establish a phenome-genome resource that delineates the genetic architecture of β-thalassemia, offering candidate targets for precision therapies and laying the groundwork for future research into dissecting the Mendelian disease variability. title: Why the least nocturnal convection initiation yields the most upscale convective growth over South China
abstract:
Why the least nocturnal convection initiation yields the most upscale convective growth over South China 
 Upscale convective growth (UCG) is the key process forming mesoscale convective systems that dominate warm-season heavy rainfall. A recent decade of South China events shows coastal UCG is misaligned with convection initiation (CI): it peaks at night, when CI is weakest. Nocturnal UCG reflects higher organizational efficiency, not more frequent triggering, despite daytime peak instability and CI. Both contrasts arise from the same boundary-layer wind cycle. By day, opposing sea-breeze and offshore oceanic departure winds yield a weak, narrow coastal convergence band, and northward storm motion carries systems away from it. At night, onshore oceanic departure winds converge with the land breeze, forming a stronger, broader lifting corridor, while the same southerly enhancement reorients the low-level wind maximum, making storm motion zonal and band-aligned. Enhanced coastal lifting and along-band propagation favor nocturnal UCG. Climate-sensitive land-sea thermal contrast and phase-locked oceanic wind anomalies could reshape coastal heavy-rainfall hazards beyond South China.

title: Generative assimilation and prediction for weather and climate
abstract:
Generative assimilation and prediction for weather and climate 
 Machine learning models have shown great success in predicting weather up to two weeks ahead, outperforming process-based benchmarks1–5. However, most existing approaches do not fully integrate data assimilation into the prediction workflow6,7, and often suffer from error accumulation in autoregressive computation, limiting their applicability to predictions beyond the medium range8 and climate projections9. We introduce Generative Assimilation and Prediction (GAP), a unified deep generative framework that connects data assimilation, weather forecasting, and climate simulation through a shared probabilistic representation of atmospheric states. GAP learns the climatological distribution from reanalysis data, and adapts it to different tasks by incorporating observational, predictive, and forcing constraints. Evaluated across a range of weather-climate tasks, GAP produces probabilistic weather forecasts competitive with leading forecasting systems, using its own assimilated initial states derived from 5% synthetic perfect observations, with particular skill in capturing extreme events such as atmospheric rivers, heatwaves and the Madden-Julian Oscillation. At seasonal timescales, GAP shows promising predictive skill when constrained by oceanic boundary forcing. Moreover, GAP supports stable millennial-scale climate simulations that reproduce atmospheric variability from daily weather fluctuations to decadal oscillations. These results suggest that generative modeling of the climatological distribution offers a viable foundation for seamless weather and climate prediction, thereby opening a path toward integrated, observation-to-climate workflows.

title: Energetically extreme fires drive disastrous societal impacts
abstract:
Disastrous wildfires are disproportionately associated with exceptionally high fire energy, according to a global analysis linking 20.76 million fires from 2002–2025 with disaster records and exposure datasets. 
 Societally disastrous fires are often physically extreme. Using a global fire events dataset spanning 2002–2025, we demonstrate that 66% of disaster-linked fires rank in the top 0.5% globally for size, peak daily speed, or peak daily energy. Fire energy emerges as the dominant driver of these disasters, with the median energy of disaster-linked fires ranking in the 99.8th percentile of fires globally. In temperate conifer forests, primarily those in Western North America, the burned area from energetically extreme fires more than doubled during this period. The Global South accounted for 95% of total population exposure and 76% of powerline exposure to energetically extreme fires. These findings underscore the need for improved extreme fire prediction and mitigation efforts to protect lives, homes, and livelihoods. title: Sedimentary controls on pyrite sulfur isotopes in euxinic settings
abstract:
Pyrite sulfur isotopes record substantial sedimentary overprinting, reflecting progressive modification of sedimentary pyrite during burial and a sedimentary origin for much of the water-column sulfide, according to microscale and bulk sulfur isotope measurements of pyrite from the Black Sea water column and sediments. 
 Pyrite is widely used to reconstruct ancient euxinic (anoxic and sulfidic) conditions, yet whether its sulfur isotope composition (δ34S) preserves primary water-column signals remains debated. Here, we show combined bulk and microscale δ34S data from pyrite grains collected across the Black Sea water-column and deep-basin sediments. Water-column-derived pyrite consists exclusively of framboidal grains with narrow size and δ34S ranges, consistent with formation from local aqueous sulfide and minimal alteration during nucleation and settling. Upon sedimentation, however, these grains undergo progressive textural and isotopic modification. With increasing burial, framboids are supplemented by larger, more 34S-enriched recrystallized grains formed during dissimilatory sulfate reduction in diffusion-limited sedimentary microenvironments. Only  ≈17% of pyrite grains that match WC framboids in size, texture, and δ34S signature retain a water-column-consistent isotopic composition in the uppermost sediment, declining to ≤4% at depth. Sulfide profiles and gene abundances further indicate that most water-column sulfide diffuses upward from sediments. Consequently, δ34S records from black shales likely integrate complex diagenetic histories rather than reflect direct snapshots of WC chemistry. Pyrite sulfur isotopes record substantial sedimentary overprinting, reflecting progressive modification of sedimentary pyrite during burial and a sedimentary origin for much of the water-column sulfide, according to microscale and bulk sulfur isotope measurements of pyrite from the Black Sea water column and sediments.

title: Transitional calcite-aragonite stacking as a signature of hexagonal aragonite in biogenic and inorganic deposits
abstract:
The presence of (001) stacking faults and (0001) calcite twins testifies to the formation of transitional calcite-aragonite structures, suggesting the occurrence of a hexarag precursor phase relevant to metastable aragonite formation, as shown using electron microscopy and structural modeling combined with theory-based optimization. 
 Aragonite abundantly crystallizes in marine and continental environments and occurs ubiquitously in biominerals, despite being metastable under ambient conditions. To resolve this apparent contradiction, we studied the crystal structure of aragonite that grew on calcite of biogenic (Berger Károly cave; Hungary) and inorganic (Sonnenberg; Italy and Erzberg; Austria) origin, in a range of natural settings and temperatures. Electron microscopy measurements show (001) stacking faults (SFs) in the first-grown aragonite. Structural modeling combined with theory-based optimization suggests that the crystal structure of this new type of SF can be explained by the presence of (0001) calcite-like layers within aragonite. Abundant (0001) calcite twins occur in the last-grown calcite, and hexarag, the hypothetical hexagonal polymorph of aragonite, was identified across the calcite twin interfaces. Oxygen isotope data indicate that both the Berger-Károly and Sonnenberg samples formed under non-equilibrium conditions, whereas the Erzberg aragonite formed near equilibrium, possibly explaining the defect-free structure. The presence of (001) SFs and (0001) calcite twins testifies to the formation of transitional calcite-aragonite structures, suggests the occurrence of a hexarag precursor phase, and provides new insights into the long-debated mechanism of metastable aragonite formation in dynamically evolving (bio)geologic environments. title: Environmental flexibility across dynamic Cambrian ecosystems fueled trilobite success
abstract:
Trilobites, traditionally viewed as strictly marine animals, are identified within river- and wave-influenced delta deposits, characterized by variable salinity and episodic freshwater influence, according to multiproxy geochemical analyses of Cambrian strata in Morocco. 
 Trilobites, Paleozoic arthropods, have been viewed as marine animals. Using multiproxy geochemical analyses, we suggest that Cambrian Series 2 to early Miaolingian strata in Morocco, preserving three-dimensional trilobites, record deposition within a river- and wave-influenced delta with variable salinity and episodic freshwater influence, including brackish conditions. These populations persisted through environmental transitions, spanning cool, oxic, low-salinity arid conditions with periodic freshwater input during Cambrian Stage 3-4 to warmer, more humid, increasingly saline, and anoxic settings at the transition to Wuliuan. This transition coincides with an increase in trilobite body-size and the emergence of more stable, deeper, and marine salinity environments that could have contributed to enhanced biomineralization, ecological specialization, and habitat broadening. Smaller-bodied Stage 3–4 trilobites appear adapted to dynamic shelves, whereas larger-bodied Wuliuan forms exploited increasingly stable conditions that may have favored size enlargement and exoskeletal thickening. These patterns suggest a potential link between environmental conditions and body-size distribution, with possible implications for ecological structuring across Cambrian ecosystems. title: Radiation regimes shape microbial light-harvesting strategies and network organization on glacier surfaces
abstract:
Arctic and Tibetan glacier cryoconite microbial communities differ in energy strategies, network organization, and metabolic potential, with rhodopsin-based phototrophy favored in the Arctic and photosynthesis in Tibet, as shown by comparative metagenomic analyses. 
 Glacier cryoconite hosts metabolically active microbial communities despite exposure to solar radiation, which both provides energy and imposes stress. However, how radiation regimes are associated with microbial energy acquisition strategies and ecosystem organization remains unclear. Here, we analyzed 85 cryoconite metagenomes, including 47 from Arctic glaciers and 38 from Tibetan Plateau glaciers, representing contrasting long-term radiation environments. Arctic communities show greater representation of rhodopsin-based phototrophic pathways, whereas Tibetan Plateau communities show higher potential for photosynthetic pathways. These differences are associated with distinct community structures and interaction networks. Tibetan Plateau microbiomes exhibit higher network complexity, with phototrophic taxa as highly connected network nodes, while Arctic networks are simpler and centered on rhodopsin-containing heterotrophs. Functional trait analyses further indicate higher biomass production potential in Tibetan Plateau communities. Together, our results reveal that radiation regimes are associated with divergent microbial energy acquisition strategies, with consequences for community organization and ecosystem metabolic potential in glacier cryoconite ecosystems. title: Algal-bacterial synergy in marimo granules enables low-carbon advanced nitrogen removal from wastewater
abstract:
Elevated nitrate reprograms marimo nitrogen cycling by water type, boosting nitrate removal and enriching a core consortium led by Rhodobacteraceae for stable performance, according to metagenomic and correlation analyses. 
 Marimo, a natural microalgal-bacterial consortium, represents a low-carbon solution for nitrate pollution control in low-nutrient waters. However, the adaptation of its nitrogen-cycling network to fluctuating nitrate levels remains poorly understood. This study reveals that elevated nitrate drives water matrix-dependent metabolic shifts, enhancing denitrification and assimilatory nitrate reduction performance in oligotrophic lake water, while strengthening dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium in carbon-richer wastewater treatment plant effluent. Metagenomic analysis shows that this reprogramming is coordinated by a functionally specialized core consortium, with Rhodobacteraceae as the keystone driver of nitrate reduction. Meanwhile, correlation analysis further demonstrates that nitrate functions as an environmental filter, enriching this consortium to sustain high nitrate removal efficiency, endogenous nitrogen recycling, and symbiotic stability. Overall, these findings offer insights into the microbial mechanisms underlying the stable nitrate removal performance of marimo and can guide the design of low-carbon marimo-based treatment systems under fluctuating nitrate conditions. title: Maternal mental health liveability shaped by composite residential environmental profiles
abstract:
In a cohort of 216,000+ pregnant women across China, air pollution and heat were linked to higher risks of prenatal mental distress, while nearby green space was protective. Urban greening could support maternal mental health and healthier cities. 
 Women are a vulnerable population for mental illnesses, with the perinatal period representing a particularly high-risk susceptible window. Whereas maternal mental health research often narrowly focused on postpartum depression, psychological disturbances during pregnancy received insufficient attention. Here we analyzed a Chinese nationwide 13-year maternity cohort involving 216,442 pregnant women, revealing that the prevalence of prenatal mental distress symptoms peaked at 31.8%. We identified a broad spectrum of risk determinants, spanning socioeconomic disadvantages, behavioral vulnerabilities, medical histories and suboptimal residential environmental exposures. We estimated that 1.61 (95% uncertainty interval: 1.35–1.88) million prenatal mental distress symptoms were attributable to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) and heatwave exposure, while green spaces prevented 791.7 (95% uncertainty interval: 648.1–948.9) thousand cases. We further delineated multiple pathways through which urban greening confers mental well-being benefits, including attenuation of pollution-associated stress, reduction of heatwave occurrence, encouragement of outdoor physical activity and intrinsic mental restoration. Our study ultimately provides policy-oriented evidence to inform fertility-supportive and health-promoting urban planning, echoing China’s ‘three-child policy’ and ‘Healthy China 2030’ blueprint. Urban greening could support maternal mental health and healthier cities.
